paragraphs: Carry these deliverable and responsibility differences into the AI impact and fit modules; this page does not infer an individual's success rate or income ranking from them.

When judging adjacent directions, the basis should be the deliverable, the scope of responsibility, and how performance is assessed: if the main deliverable is media or service sales, compare advertising sales agents; if it is research design and interpretation, compare market research analysts; if you are responsible only for one campaign's material and placement, return to the advertising and promotions manager sub-basis; if you own regional or team sales targets, compare sales managers; if it centres on reputation and public communication, compare public relations managers; if it centres on cross-team process improvement, compare management analysts.
Also a management role, but its deliverable focuses on a single launchable campaign and does not cover pricing or product-mix decisions.
If you prefer campaign planning, material and media coordination, and are willing to be accountable for placement results, learn about this sub-direction first.
Plan, direct, or coordinate advertising policies and programmes, produce promotional material, coordinate media and budget, and review campaign performance.
Advertising and promotions managers (O*NET 11-2011.00)
Assessed mainly on closing and client relationships, without deciding how a campaign is organized or placed.
If you prefer client development, negotiation, and sales targets and are willing to carry performance pressure, learn about this direction.
Sell media space or advertising services to clients: develop clients, prepare proposals and quotes, negotiate, and follow up on placement and renewals.
Advertising sales agents (O*NET 41-3011.00)
Delivers research design and interpretation without responsibility for budget execution or team management.
If you prefer methods, data, and interpretation and want decisions driven by evidence, learn about this direction.
Design and execute market and audience research, collect and analyse data, and deliver conclusions and recommendations.
Market research analysts and marketing specialists (O*NET 13-1161.00)
Delivered as sales organization and channel results, with a smaller marketing-mix decision scope than a marketing manager.
If you prefer team metric management and client relationships and are willing to carry sales team responsibility, learn about this direction.
Set regional or team sales targets, manage the sales process, people, and client relationships, and be accountable for results.
Sales managers (O*NET 11-2022.00)
Centred on reputation and public communication; the main deliverable is not paid advertising or a marketing-mix plan.
If you prefer media relations, issues management, and crisis communication, learn about this direction.
Manage the organization's external image and communication, handling media relations, agenda setting, and crisis communication.
Public relations managers (O*NET 11-2032.00)
Delivered as process and organizational improvement, usually without owning the marketing budget or launch decision.
If you prefer process diagnosis and organizational improvement rather than market growth goals, learn about this direction.
Diagnose organizational or process problems, propose improvements, and support implementation and evaluation.
Management analysts (O*NET 13-1111.00)
Choose a direction by the deliverable you want to own: a launchable campaign, a sale, a research conclusion, a regional result, or a full marketing-mix plan.

entries: Able to explain the basis for a judgment from customer demand, the competitive landscape, and financial constraints.

paragraphs: Treating interest codes as a hiring or ability threshold will misjudge people who are unsuited; return instead to real tasks, budget conditions, and how performance is assessed.

Big Five results can suggest work habits; the occupational material checked for this page establishes no predictive relationship between scores and individual work performance. Observe plan version management, budget boundaries, and cross-team communication, and explore with a complete marketing plan and review record.

entries: Able to complete the market analysis table and plan on the template and write the assumptions, limits, and uncertainty clearly.
Under multi-party feedback and quarterly assessment pressure, still able to complete plan versions and budget records through the approval process.

paragraphs: Using scores in place of task evidence leads to misjudgment: a low score does not mean poor performance, and a high score does not guarantee driving multi-party collaboration; judge by the plan, budget, and review quality.

Start by checking your interest with one simulated plan: complete the target customer judgment, three verifiable claims, one pricing or channel assumption, and a one-page review, then see whether you are willing to revise repeatedly based on data. O*NET lists marketing managers' interest code as EC; it describes preferences for work environments and does not guarantee hiring outcomes or job performance.

MBTI can serve as preference reflection; this page found no evidence that it predicts individual performance in this occupation. Record actual performance in structured analysis, written communication, and open discussion, and explore through plan review and review feedback, rather than judging competence by type.

Enterprising E corresponds to influencing, negotiating, and driving decisions, and Conventional C to organizing information and data by rules; both point to real market judgment and planning work rather than a judgment of personal ability.
EC

entries: Able to keep plan versions and data sources consistent amid multi-party feedback.
Leaves room for pricing and investment assumptions to be disproved by data rather than locking the plan in too early.

paragraphs: Enterprising E + Conventional C (EC)
Treating MBTI type as a hiring standard leads to faulty screening; judge instead by plan reviews, budget execution, and review-session performance.

The Enneagram describes motivational tendencies, and fit with this occupation can only be verified through tasks. It can help you reflect on how you react to performance pressure, budget cuts, and cross-department disagreement, but it cannot infer professional ability; check it against simulated plans and review records.

entries: When a plan falls short of expectations, able to check the data basis and execution first, then decide whether to adjust or stop.
In reviews, records the basis for one's own judgments and the reasons for changes rather than continuing the next round of investment on impression alone.

paragraphs: Treating type as a necessary job requirement causes misjudgment; motivational tendencies do not determine work outcomes, so verifiable task behavior should govern.

Start with market share, cost structure, unit economics, and percentage change; pricing, statistics, and analysis roles may need deeper mathematical or coding ability, which must be checked against the duties. This page establishes no predictive relationship between an IQ score and hiring or work quality in this occupation, and actual ability can be recorded through budget modelling and data interpretation.

entries: Able to read acquisition cost, conversion rate, and gross margin and adjust investment judgments accordingly.
Able to check budget allocation against contract amounts and identify data that is not on a consistent basis.

paragraphs: This page does not use an IQ score to judge fit or entry; specific positions also require checking analysis, communication, decision-making, and people-management tasks, and the ability requirement cannot be reduced to number reading.

An emotional ability self-rating can be used to reflect on cross-team and client communication; this page did not verify the predictive power of its score for performance in this occupation. The editorial suggestion is to record how you clarify the goal, communicate, and review when a plan is rejected, performance falls, or a review is public; these records are also not sufficient on their own to judge long-term competence.

entries: When a plan is rejected or performance is unfavourable, able to confirm the goal and the data first, then adjust the plan.
Able to notice one's own reactions in a high-pressure review and seek another person's check rather than carrying it alone.

paragraphs: This page does not use an emotional intelligence score to judge hiring or fit; review, feedback handling, and review performance can be recorded, but this page did not verify the predictive power of these materials or scores for long-term work outcomes.
Advertising and promotions managers
Want the deliverable to focus on a single launchable, reviewable advertising or promotional campaign.

Mainly focuses on advertising and promotional projects but may take part in marketing strategy and product development coordination; pricing and product-mix authority must be checked against the specific position and cannot be ruled out absolutely.
Market research analysts
Prefer using research design and data to answer audience and channel questions.
Delivers conclusions and recommendations without responsibility for budget execution or team management.
Sales manager
Willing to be accountable for regional or team sales targets and people management.
Delivered as sales organization and channel results, with a smaller marketing-mix decision scope.
Advertising sales agents
Want client development and closing as the main goal and to carry performance pressure.
Mainly focuses on the sales organization and closing; the degree of involvement in marketing plans or pricing must be checked against the position, and no absolute mutual exclusion is established.
Public relations managers
Willing to work around media relations, issues, and reputation communication.
Focuses on public communication and crisis response and does not carry the marketing budget for paid advertising.
Product manager
Want to work around product definition, requirement prioritisation, and launch timing.

The product direction may involve product definition, requirement prioritisation, and launch timing; the specific R&D roadmap, communications, and budget authority are divided by duties. Willing to judge demand and competition with data and drive cross-team delivery within budget and compliance boundaries.
Be cautious if you expect to do only creative execution without dealing with budgets and people issues, or are unwilling to face quarterly performance assessment.
